title: A phone remote made for your thumb
question: Choose a direction. Each keeps the touchpad first and typing/tabs separate.

options.label: After hours
options.thesis: A quiet, spacious remote with browsing always within reach.
options.viewport: Compact page title, a large touchpad, quick actions and a bottom Remote/Type/Tabs bar.
options.risk: The understated identity depends on precise spacing and excellent feedback.

raised.raise: Every control and status gets decisive contrast; decoration is removed.
The active task and current tab stay visually unmistakable.
Status changes remain legible without rearranging the controls.

options.label: Soft charcoal
options.thesis: A warmer, tactile-looking remote with a generous touch surface.
options.viewport: A compact identity above a warm-plum pad, with a clear Click action and separate task views.
options.risk: Familiar and comfortable; this is the closest option to conventional premium remote apps.

options.label: Clear blue
options.thesis: Flat, decisive controls with a blue active-control field.
options.viewport: Compact fixed-size page identity, plain touchpad, crisp square-edged actions and obvious task selection.
options.risk: Stronger contrast and flatter shapes may feel more assertive.
options.case: Strong task clarity; the calmer assigned direction better suits sustained couch use.

options.label: Night wayfinding
options.thesis: Precise blue controls and a continuous active-task marker.
options.viewport: Live identity and clear connection state above the pad; task navigation and quick actions remain anchored.
options.risk: More structured and denser than After hours.
options.case: Familiar wayfinding helps orientation; the assigned direction gives the pad more breathing room.

options.label: Data field
options.thesis: The remote remains touchpad-first with standard web controls.
options.viewport: Page identity, touchpad and quick actions.
options.risk: Dense numeric/bar fields provide no useful content for this pointer-first remote.
options.case: Dense numeric/bar fields provide no useful content for this pointer-first remote.
options.kept: Decisive contrast and removal of decoration.

options.label: Streaming shelf
options.thesis: The remote remains touchpad-first with standard web controls.
options.viewport: Page identity, touchpad and quick actions.
options.risk: The remote exposes tab titles, not a poster-art catalog; adding poster tiles would imply unsupported content.
options.case: The remote exposes tab titles, not a poster-art catalog; adding poster tiles would imply unsupported content.
options.kept: Unmistakable active task and selected-tab identity.

options.label: Timetable rack
options.thesis: The remote remains touchpad-first with standard web controls.
options.viewport: Page identity, touchpad and quick actions.
options.risk: Raked glass and one-size typography weaken quick-control readability on a narrow phone.
options.case: Raked glass and one-size typography weaken quick-control readability on a narrow phone.
options.kept: Consistent spacing and readable fixed-size labels.

options.label: Gate board
options.thesis: The remote remains touchpad-first with standard web controls.
options.viewport: Page identity, touchpad and quick actions.
options.risk: An ordered departure board has no true equivalent in the gesture-first task.
options.case: An ordered departure board has no true equivalent in the gesture-first task.
options.kept: State changes stay legible without moving controls.

canonCard.label: Familiar remote
canonCard.thesis: Standard mobile remote conventions with careful proportions.
canonCard.viewport: Compact top identity, large plain touchpad, quick controls and three bottom task tabs.
canonCard.risk: A familiar appearance rather than a distinctive visual identity.
